request.spec:
Show me the name of the person with the highest influence on the sheet. If two people tie, pick
the one whose name comes first alphabetically.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for this implementation's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show me the name of the person with the highest influence on the sheet. If two people tie, pick
the one whose name comes first alphabetically.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now shows a "Top influence" line with the name of the person who has the highest influence. If two people tie, the name that comes first alphabetically wins. Both Playwright tests pass in `bin/e2e`: the normal case shows "Kai" and the tie case shows "Alan".

The change is all in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`, as a new `topInfluence` value next to the other sheet totals. The server already works out each person's influence, so nothing else needed to change.

- **Nobody to pick:** if no one on the sheet has an influence value, the line shows "n/a", matching how "Leader" behaves.
- **Missing influence:** people whose influence is "n/a" are left out of the comparison.
- **Alphabetical order:** names are compared with the browser's normal language-aware sort. This means differences in upper and lower case are ordered the way a reader would expect, rather than by raw character codes.
